name: Find eyewitness YouTube footage of breaking events with OpenAI, Google Sheets and Telegram

parameters.content:
## Find eyewitness YouTube footage of breaking events with OpenAI, Google Sheets and Telegram

### How it works

This workflow lets a newsroom open monitoring windows for breaking events, then periodically searches recent YouTube results for eyewitness-style footage. It stores event definitions and discovered videos in Google Sheets, scores and optionally classifies candidates with OpenAI, and sends Telegram digests plus operational alerts. Form submissions create new events, while scheduled or manual runs read active events, search and paginate through results, deduplicate against the footage log, update event status, and notify the desk.

### Setup steps

- Configure Google Sheets credentials and prepare the spreadsheet tabs used for Events and Footage Log with the columns expected by the code nodes.
- Configure Telegram bot credentials and set the target chat ID in the Set Desk Config node.
- Configure OpenAI credentials for the OpenAI Chat Model sub-node if AI title classification should be used.
- Set the search API endpoint/key used by the Search YouTube Last Hour HTTP Request node, and verify rate limits match the wait/pagination settings.
- Review Set Desk Config values such as sheetUrl, telegramChatId, formats, defaultWindowHours, and any maximum event-window settings in the code nodes.

### Customization

Adjust the search formats, query-building rules, scoring thresholds, AI prompt/labels, polling schedule, Telegram digest formatting, and event-window length to fit the newsroom’s beat and urgency.

## Start and route run

Entry triggers for form, scheduled, and manual runs converge into shared desk configuration, then branch based on whether the run came from a new event form submission or a monitoring cycle.

## Create event record

Handles the upper form-submission branch by converting submitted event details into an Events sheet row, saving it, announcing monitoring in Telegram, and showing either success or save-failure feedback to the submitter.

## Load sheet state

Reads the active event list and existing footage log from Google Sheets for monitoring runs, with a nearby Telegram alert path if either sheet read fails.

## Plan search jobs

Builds search jobs and event-closing updates from the sheet data, then starts the batch loop that processes each search query and format.

## Prepare page request

Creates the request parameters for the first or next result page and decides whether a given search should be skipped before calling the external search service.

## Call YouTube search

Adds a short delay for rate limiting, then calls the recent YouTube search API for the current search job page.

## Handle search pages

Evaluates returned search results, decides whether to fetch another page, and converts failed HTTP requests into loop-safe failure markers so the batch can continue.

## Score candidate videos

After the search loop completes, merges results, removes videos already present in the footage log, applies rule-based scores, and decides whether AI classification is needed.

## Classify titles with AI

Uses an OpenAI-backed LLM chain to classify candidate video titles when the workflow is configured to use AI enrichment.

## Build footage rows

Applies AI labels or falls back to rule labels, prepares footage-log rows and run summary data, then branches based on whether there are new videos to write.

## Write footage log

Splits new video rows, appends them to the Footage Log sheet, and restores the single run summary after the sheet write returns row-level items.

## Update event rows

Checks whether any event records need status or window updates, splits those event rows, and writes the updates back to the Events tab.

## Send final notifications

Builds and sends the Telegram run digest, while the nearby error node reports sheet write failures from footage or event updates.

assignments.name: footageTerms
assignments.value: footage, caught on camera, eyewitness, filmed, dashcam, cctv, raw video, my window, right now, happening now, just happened, video shows, moment

assignments.name: newsTerms
assignments.value: news, breaking news, live coverage, bulletin, press conference, reporter, update, updates, tv

assignments.name: commentaryTerms
assignments.value: reaction, reacts, explained, analysis, opinion, podcast, prayer, compilation, documentary, what we know

assignments.name: aiRubric
assignments.value:
You support a newsroom verification desk during a breaking event. For each YouTube video, decide which category fits best, judging only from the title, channel name and format:
- eyewitness: likely filmed by someone present (phone video, dashcam, CCTV, view from a window or street, raw clip with little editing). Short raw titles that name a place are often eyewitness.
- news_reupload: a TV or news broadcast, a live news stream, a press conference, or a channel reposting other people's footage.
- commentary: reaction, analysis, explainer, opinion, prayer, compilation or podcast.
- unrelated: not about this event (same word, different topic, or clearly another time or place).
When unsure between eyewitness and news_reupload, prefer news_reupload. Write the reason in English, max 15 words.
